analytic_obligations.degree-setting: The chosen form is Gauduchon; no d-closed hypothesis is imposed.

analytic_obligations.metric-ratio: Two determinant metrics have a global positive ratio exp(f).

analytic_obligations.sheaf-determinant: The determinant of a positive-rank torsion-free sheaf on smooth X is a line bundle; this standard coherent-sheaf fact is accepted.
analytic_obligations.stability-tests: Only subsheaves of intermediate positive rank with torsion-free quotient are tested, as in Jacob Definition5.
analytic_obligations.rank-one: There are no intermediate-rank tests for a line bundle.
analytic_obligations.theta-zero: At theta=0 all subsheaves are preserved and the commutator term vanishes.
analytic_obligations.indecomposability: A holomorphic splitting into two nonzero bundles contradicts stability: the two smaller slopes cannot have the total slope as their weighted average.
analytic_obligations.classic-existence: Li--Yau existence for stable locally free bundles on compact Gauduchon manifolds is an explicit accepted classical input; no original full proof is certified.
analytic_obligations.jacob-conversion: Jacob degree divides by (n-1)! and volume by n!; their ratio gives the book factor n. Multiplying slopes by a common positive factor preserves stability.
analytic_obligations.constant-sign: Positive degree, rank and omega volume force the Einstein constant positive.
analytic_obligations.complement-bound: Positive mean gives one positive directional curvature eigenvalue, so the retained exhaustion gives n+r-1.
analytic_obligations.product-factors: Each factor separately has positive definite Einstein mean; no product stability is needed.
analytic_obligations.product-vectors: The retained tensor trace theorem covers every vector, including nondecomposable tensors.
analytic_obligations.product-count: There is one positive tangent eigenvalue per independent tangent block, giving n+r-k.
analytic_obligations.flat-metric: Fix the specified unitary flat Chern metric before choosing disc and sphere radii.
analytic_obligations.compact-exception: Compact K in the complement stays uniformly away from the removed zero section.
analytic_obligations.parallel-frames: Flat unitary Chern connections have parallel holomorphic unitary frames on simply connected patches.
analytic_obligations.sphere-descent: Constant unitary transitions preserve the sphere and its probability measure.
analytic_obligations.average-smooth: The sphere is compact and psi smooth, so derivatives commute with the local integral.
analytic_obligations.horizontal-positivity: The constant nonzero sphere vectors define holomorphic horizontal sections; their Hessians are strictly positive.
analytic_obligations.maximum-contradiction: A smooth function on a positive-dimensional compact complex manifold cannot have positive definite complex Hessian everywhere.
analytic_obligations.hopf-parameters: n>=2 and real q,a in (0,1); the deck action is free and properly discontinuous.
analytic_obligations.curvature-sign: b<0, so the normalized curvature -b alpha is semipositive.
analytic_obligations.curvature-rank: Cauchy--Schwarz gives the radial kernel Cz and n-1 strictly positive directions.
analytic_obligations.elliptic-fibres: The projectivization map has compact embedded fibres C*/q^Z.
analytic_obligations.restricted-curvature: On each lifted fibre log|zeta|^2 is pluriharmonic, so the Chern connection of the restricted metric is flat.
analytic_obligations.closed-restriction: The restricted projective complement is a closed complex submanifold; restricting an exhaustion remains proper.
analytic_obligations.lower-index: Strict positivity survives restriction outside the compact intersection, contradicting the flat-bundle lemma.
analytic_obligations.hopf-topology: The scalar real contraction translates log radius, so X is S^(2n-1) times S1.
analytic_obligations.vanishing-de-Rham: For n>=2 the sphere has no degree1/2 cohomology; the product has H2=0.
analytic_obligations.positive-degree: A nonzero semipositive (1,1) form has strictly positive wedge with any positive (n-1) power.
